title: policy-driven failover: runbooks-as-helm-operator + terraform cross-az lb
author: Priya Nair
description: This PR introduces a policy-driven failover automation stack for private deployments: a lightweight Helm operator that surfaces 'runbooks-as-code' as Kubernetes CRs and executes them safely (prechecks, dry-run, gated step progression), plus a Terraform module and Helm chart changes to support cross-AZ load-balancer failover and restore hooks. Motivation: customers running Redwood Private in VPC/on-prem clusters asked for an automated, auditable failover workflow that can be triggered manually or by alerting playbooks and that can be rehearsed as code. What changed: 1) new component 'runbook-operator' Helm chart (charts/runbook-operator) and CRD + controller to run templated runbooks as Jobs, capture step outputs to S3-compatible store, and emit events/metrics; 2) new terraform module 'tf-modules/dr-network' that creates cross-AZ LB configs, health-checks, and an optional floating VIP via metalLB or cloud provider API; 3) installer hooks: pre-upgrade and post-upgrade DR validation jobs wired into the private-installer Helm umbrella charts; 4) runbooks/ directory with canonical DR playbooks (failover, failback, partial-az-evacuation, etc.) expressed as YAML with parameter schemas and test fixtures; 5) upgrade/rollback tool improvements: 'installer rollback --dr-validate' flag that runs the operator's post-checks and can auto-open a rollback ticket; 6) E2E canary job and chaos script used in CI to validate failover paths. Backwards compatibility: operator is optional and gated by values.runbookOperator.enabled=false by default. Testing: unit+integration for controller logic, e2e on a 3-AZ kine cluster, and a smoke terraform plan/apply in CI. Checklist: - [x] Helm chart and CRD design reviewed - [x] Terraform module interfaces documented - [x] Migration guide added to docs/private-dr.md - [x] Smoke e2e and CI jobs added - [x] Security review for S3 credential handling completed Rollout plan: staged canary in Dedicated -> Private trial customers -> general availability. Related: ENG-4821 (DR runbook operator), ENG-4897 (installer failover hooks), SUP-9112 (customer incident that motivated automated failover).
commits: terraform: dr-network module for cross-az lb and healthchecks
installer: wire pre/post upgrade hooks to runbook operator
docs: add private-dr.md and migration notes
tests: add e2e canary and chaos script
ci: add dr-canary workflow and terraform smoke job
diff_snippets:
--- templates/crd-runbook.yaml +++
+apiVersion: infra.redwood.ai/v1
+kind: Runbook
+metadata:
+  name: failover-full-az
+spec:
+  parametersSchema: {}
  
+resource "metal_lb_virtual_ip" "dr_vip" {
+  count = var.enable_vip ? 1 : 0
+  address = var.vip_address
+}
+values.yaml snippet: runbookOperator:
+  enabled: true
+  s3:
+    endpoint: "{{ .Values.s3.endpoint }}"
+    bucket: "redwood-dr-logs"
review_thread: Liam Chen: Can the operator run steps in parallel? Concern about locking when multiple playbooks reference same resources.
Priya Nair: Operator supports step-level locking via a lightweight ConfigMap mutex; parallelism is opt-in per-runbook. Added tests for concurrent runs.
Marisol Ortega: Terraform module needs clearer inputs for cloud vs metal deployments.
Priya Nair: Added variable 'provider_mode' and example files for aws/gcp/onprem; documented in README.
Noah Patel: CI flaked once on e2e when chaos injected network partition too early; recommend adding a readiness wait.
Priya Nair: Added readiness probe and extended wait in chaos script; re-ran canary and CI is green.
release_notes:
- Add runbook-operator Helm chart to run DR playbooks as Kubernetes CRs and Jobs.
- Introduce terraform module 'dr-network' for cross-AZ LB and optional VIP.
- Installer hooks for pre/post-upgrade DR validation and rollback gating.
- New canonical runbooks for failover/failback rehearsals.
- CI canary workflow to validate failover paths before rollout.
